name: Computer Networks - IP Networking, Routing & TCP
description: IP addressing, subnetting, ARP, DHCP, fragmentation, ICMP, distance-vector & link-state routing, BGP, and TCP congestion control (CCN05-CCN07)

questions.question: Given IP 192.168.10.130/26, what is the network address?
How many usable host addresses are available in a /27 subnet?
Which of the following IP ranges is a private address range?
What is the broadcast address of the subnet 192.168.1.64/27?
Which statement about ARP cache entries is TRUE?
options: They are statically configured and never expire
They are dynamically learned and timed out after a period
They are broadcast to all hosts on the network periodically
They are stored on the DNS server

questions.question: When a host sends an ARP request, which devices process it?
options: Only the router on the subnet
All devices on the local broadcast domain
Only devices matching the target IP

questions.question: What is the subnet mask for a /22 network?
A host wants to reach 8.8.8.8, which is outside its subnet. Which MAC address will ARP resolve?
options: The MAC of the DNS server
The MAC of the default gateway
ARP is not used for off-subnet destinations

questions.question: In IP fragmentation, which statement is TRUE about the More Fragments (MF) flag?
options: MF = 1 for the last fragment only
MF = 1 for all fragments including the last
MF = 1 for all fragments except the last

questions.question: If MTU = 1,000 bytes and IP header = 20 bytes, what is the maximum data payload per fragment (except the last)?
Which IP packet field is used to correctly reassemble fragmented IP packets at the destination?
Which situation will NOT generate an ICMP error message?
options: Packet exceeds MTU with DF bit set
Packet sent to a broadcast or multicast address

questions.question: A router receives a packet larger than the MTU with the DF (Don't Fragment) bit set to 1. What happens?
options: The router fragments the packet normally
The router drops the packet silently
The router drops the packet and sends an ICMP Type 3 Code 4 message to the source
The router sends the packet on a higher-MTU alternative path

questions.question: An ICMP error message includes which of the following?
options: The original IP header plus the first 8 bytes of the original payload
Only the destination IP address of the failed packet

questions.question: When TTL becomes 0 at a router, what occurs?
options: The packet is forwarded with TTL reset to 64
The router requests a retransmission from the source
The packet is dropped and an ICMP Time Exceeded message is sent to the source
The packet is held until TTL is refreshed

questions.question: A DHCP Discover message is sent as:
options: Unicast to the known DHCP server
Broadcast to all devices on the network
Multicast to the DHCP group address
Anycast to the nearest DHCP server

questions.question: DHCP uses which UDP port numbers?
What does a DHCP relay agent do?
options: Assigns IP addresses locally without a server
Caches DHCP responses to speed up future requests
Forwards client DHCP broadcasts as unicast to a DHCP server on another subnet
Converts DHCP requests into DNS queries

questions.question: A router is computing shortest paths from node D. The current tentative distances are: B = 11, C = 2. Which node will be added next to the confirmed set?
options: Neither until the full graph is known

questions.question: In a link-state routing system, a link between two routers fails. What is the correct system behavior?
options: Only the directly connected routers update their tables
Routing loops form until manual intervention
A new link-state update is flooded to all routers, which then recompute paths
BGP sends a withdrawal to all peers

questions.question: A router receives a link-state packet from a neighbor. To which neighbors should it forward this packet?
options: To all neighbors including the sender
To no neighbors; link-state packets are not forwarded
To all neighbors except the one it came from
Only to neighbors with lower routing costs

questions.question: A router receives two identical link-state packets from the same source with the same sequence number. What should it do?
options: Keep one and discard the duplicate
Request a newer update from the source

questions.question: Why do link-state routing protocols avoid long-term routing loops?
options: They use split horizon to prevent loops
All routers compute consistent shortest-path trees from the same topology database
They periodically reset all routing tables
Sequence numbers prevent any packet from being forwarded twice

questions.question: Why does hierarchical routing reduce routing table size?
options: It uses compression on routing table entries
It groups destinations into regions, requiring only regional-level entries for remote destinations
It eliminates the need for default routes
It replaces dynamic routing with static routes

questions.question: A TCP connection has cwnd = 64 KB and RTT = 80 ms. What is the approximate maximum throughput?

A TCP connection has cwnd = 24 MSS. A timeout occurs. What are the new cwnd and ssthresh?
A TCP connection has cwnd = 30 MSS and a triple duplicate ACK occurs. What are the new cwnd and ssthresh after fast recovery?
A link has bandwidth = 100 Mbps and RTT = 50 ms. What is the bandwidth-delay product (required window size)?
In TCP, reliability is achieved using byte numbering through sequence numbers, confirmation using acknowledgments, and recovery using:

Why is fast recovery preferable to timeout-based recovery in TCP?
options: Fast recovery uses forward error correction to fix errors
Fast recovery avoids resetting cwnd to 1 MSS, maintaining higher throughput
Fast recovery eliminates the need for retransmissions
Fast recovery only applies to UDP flows

questions.question: Why is TCP window scaling necessary in high-speed networks?
options: IPv6 requires a larger window field
The default 16-bit window size is too small for the bandwidth-delay product of high-speed links
Window scaling enables TLS encryption of TCP options
It allows TCP to operate over UDP tunnels

questions.question: Two TCP flows share a link with RTTs of 20 ms and 200 ms. Which flow receives more bandwidth under standard TCP Reno?
A TCP flow over a 10 Gbps link with RTT = 100 ms achieves only 200 Mbps. What is the primary limitation?
TCP exits slow start when:
options: A triple duplicate ACK is received

questions.question: A receiver advertises a zero window and later frees buffer space, but the connection remains stalled. What is the most likely cause?
options: The sender's cwnd has been reset to 1 MSS
The server has closed the connection
The window update packet was lost and the persist timer failed

questions.question: In IP fragmentation, a 4,000-byte IP packet (including 20-byte header) is sent over a link with MTU = 1,020 bytes. How many fragments are created?
Which of the following most accurately describes the difference between distance vector and link-state routing?
options: Distance vector uses Dijkstra; link-state uses Bellman-Ford
Distance vector routers know the full topology; link-state routers only know neighbors
Distance vector can suffer from count-to-infinity; link-state avoids this with complete topology knowledge
Link-state scales better to small networks; distance vector to large ones

questions.question: A TCP sender is in congestion avoidance with cwnd = 20 MSS. After 5 RTTs with no loss, what is cwnd?
Which field in an IP packet is decremented by each router and causes the packet to be discarded when it reaches zero?
During DHCP lease renewal (at the T1 timer), the client sends its renewal request to:
options: The original DHCP server via unicast

questions.question: Why is subnetting used in IP networking?
options: To increase the total number of available IP addresses
To organize networks and reduce broadcast domain size
To eliminate the need for routing between departments

questions.question: Traceroute works because:
options: It reads the routing table of each intermediate router
Routers send ICMP Time Exceeded messages when TTL expires in transit
It uses a special UDP port that routers intercept
Each router appends its address to the packet
